subject: Quick recap + TTFT/streaming targets (Finlytics / Redwood)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + TTFT/streaming targets (Finlytics / Redwood)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the performance SLOs you called out.

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary UX requirement: streaming responses to the client (progressive render) via SSE or WebSocket.
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target <= 200ms at 99th percentile (goal: <= 150ms if possible).
- Chunk cadence: ideally <= 100ms between chunks for smooth streaming; acceptable up to 150ms for some endpoints.
- Concurrency: expected peak concurrency ~200 concurrent streams, burst to 350.
- Throughput: baseline ~50 req/s sustained across the service, spiky bursts to ~120 req/s during peak minutes.
- End-to-end constraint: your product team expects overall UI render of first content within 300ms of user click (includes network and client rendering).

What Redwood needs from you to validate/size:
1) A traffic sample (simple JSON payloads and expected response sizes) — attached sample file works.
2) Confirmation on preferred streaming protocol (SSE vs WebSocket) and whether the client can tolerate chunk cadence variance.
3) Any network path constraints (mobile carriers, specific CDNs) that add latency.

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep-dive: 60–90min call with Marissa (SE) to go through traffic profile and run an initial sizing/PoC plan. Suggested slots: Tue 2027-06-01 10:00 or Wed 2027-06-02 14:00 PT — please confirm what works.
- We will run a 1-hour synthetic load test on a dedicated pool (if you want dedicated) or hosted with reserved capacity to validate TTFT and chunk cadence.
- Deliverable: short SLO proposal (attached: redwood-ttft-slo-proposal.pdf) detailing expected 50/90/99p TTFT and recommended deployment mode.

Attachments: redwood-ttft-slo-proposal.pdf, finlytics-traffic-samples.json

If that sounds right, confirm the sync time and we’ll block Marissa.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

----
From previous call notes (for context):
- Finlytics wants to prioritize low-latency streaming on web and mobile.
- Regulatory/PII: data is tokenized at the client, and payloads are JSON without PHI.

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finlytics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + TTFT/streaming targets (Finlytics / Redwood)

Thanks Aditya — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:  

- Confirmed: SSE is our preferred path for web due to existing client infra, but we can do WebSocket for mobile if needed.
- TTFT: our product team is aiming for 150ms 99p TTFT as a stretch target, 200ms is the maximum acceptable.
- Chunk cadence: we actually preferred ~50–75ms between chunks for the main feed (very visual). If that's not feasible, 100ms is acceptable for secondary endpoints.
- Concurrency/throughput: your numbers align with our telemetry. Important: sustained 50 req/s but our spikes can be bursty — sometimes 200 req/s for 20–30s when multiple users navigate.

We attached the API spec and a small sample of payloads. Also, one more constraint: we run some inference through an internal proxy that adds ~20–40ms; please include that in any end-to-end modeling.

Let's do the tech sync — Tue 2027-06-01 10:00 PT works for our team (I'll send a calendar invite). Please confirm Marissa can join and whether you want any pre-reads.

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product, Finlytics
alex.j@finlytics.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + TTFT/streaming targets (Finlytics / Redwood)

Perfect — thanks for the quick confirmation, Alex. Marissa and I will be on the sync Tue 2027-06-01 10:00 PT. I added a short pre-read to the shared doc (link below) that outlines what we’ll validate during the call:

Proposed tech-sync agenda (60 min)
- 5m: introductions and goals
- 10m: Finlytics traffic profile and key endpoints (Alex)
- 20m: Redwood runtime behavior for streaming (Marissa) — TTFT drivers, batching, KV caching, network RTT assumptions
- 15m: Sizing & PoC plan (Aditya/Marissa) — dedicated vs hosted, test harness, metrics to capture (TTFT p50/p90/p99, chunk cadence distribution, CPU/GPU utilization)
- 10m: Q&A and next steps (action items + owners)

What we’ll bring to the call:
- Preliminary SLO projections: we expect TTFT p50 ~ 70–110ms, p90 ~ 120–160ms, and p99 typically ~140–220ms depending on model size and quantization. Those are for a hosted configuration with workload-aware batching and prefix caching. Dedicated pools usually improve p99 by ~10–30% under the same config.
- Chunk cadence: with SSE/WebSocket we can target median chunk cadence ~40–80ms; 99p cadence depends on client network jitter and can be >150ms on poor mobile carriers.
- Test plan: 1-hour synthetic run + 15min burst test; we’ll capture TTFT at the ingress and after proxy to model your 20–40ms proxy overhead.

Action items before the call:
- Alex: upload a 2–5 minute traffic sample (finlytics-traffic-samples.json attached) and confirm which endpoints need 50–75ms cadence.
- Aditya/Marissa: prepare short SLO proposal and preliminary sizing (redwood-ttft-slo-proposal.pdf).

Related doc (pre-read): https://docs.google.com/document/d/finlytics-ttft-proposal
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/FIN-2027-0421

Looking forward to the call. If anything changes on timing, let me know and we’ll adjust.

Best,
Aditya Rao
